title: Coherent strict quotient presentation of every good complex
statement: Fix a prime l, a finite coefficient extension E/Q_l, any scheme Y, a coefficient derived system calculus S [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], and a flat-term K-flat completed-coefficient complex P. There exist a strict sequence-site complex C, an isomorphism e from S.reduction(Q(P)) to Q(C), and simultaneous chain isomorphisms kappa from each evaluation of C to the actual termwise finite tensor reduction of P, satisfying CoefficientReductionPresentation and IsIntegralComparisonPresentationCoherent [def-trf-integral-comparison-realization-models]. The latter fixes e through the two adjunction Hom bijections as the localization of the strict tensor-unit tower map specified by kappa. Site and coefficient universes are independent; no geometric invertibility, constructibility or boundedness assumption is imposed.

source.place: Tags 06YY (derived tensor), 07A6 (lemma-adjoint), 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok), and derived.tex lemma-derived-adjoint-functors (09T5); canonical quotient-presentation substep of lem-trf-primitive-quotient-realizations-unique.

proof.text: Choose the existing ordinary quotient-system tensor/limit model M. Apply its tensor functor termwise to P, obtaining C. The mapped finite evaluation isomorphisms give kappa; M.transition proves every horizontal presentation equation degreewise.

Use the existing canonical termwise-limit comparison and normalized constant-limit derived unit. The resolving-class helpers of the derived-adjunction comparison module derive M.tensor and its adjunction to coefficientSequenceLimit. Transport the resulting comparison to the given S.reduction using uniqueness of left adjoints. It is invertible on P. The transported Hom formula identifies its transpose with the localized ordinary unit followed by the actual composite right-derived unit. Apply finiteComparison_of_unit to obtain every normalized finite presentation equation.

Transpose the ordinary complex unit through the constant-tower/ordinary-limit adjunction to obtain the strict tower map b. M.unit_tensor, the inverse finite evaluation isomorphism, and equality transports on section types give the prescribed formula for b. Apply the derived adjunction counit factorization and the exact localization comparison to its Hom formula. The two termwise-limit identifications coincide by their projections, so cancel. Naturality of the derived diagonal-limit counit gives exactly the entire-tower equation of IsIntegralComparisonPresentationCoherent. No finite derived evaluation is used to detect an equality. The zero complex, n=0 (exponent one), and arbitrary schemes use the same universal properties.

lean.statement:
theorem coherentPrimitiveReductionPresentation {Y : Scheme.{t}}
    (S : CoefficientDerivedSystemCalculus l E Y)
    (P : (integralOperationsGoodComplex l E Y).FullSubcategory) :
    ∃ (C : CochainComplex (coefficientSequenceModules l E Y) ℤ)
      (e : S.reduction.obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P.obj) ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj C)
      (κ : ∀ n : ℕ,
        ((coefficientSequenceEvaluation l E Y n).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj C ≅
          (unrestrictedIntegralFiniteComplex l E Y n).obj P.obj),
      CoefficientReductionPresentation l E Y S.toCoefficientDerivedSystemReduction
        P.obj P.property.1 C e κ ∧
      IsIntegralComparisonPresentationCoherent l E Y S P.obj C e κ
